**Service denied:** Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
**Treating surgeon:** Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026, effective 2026-08-04 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-313%20Hip%20Replace%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

## Why I am writing

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), denied by Cigna on 2026-08-09 under reference number POC-4E415360FE-32022. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records already in my chart contain the clinical detail the plan's own guideline calls for. In the sections below I set that documentation out point by point, so that nothing has to be searched for.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-05, which is 180 days from the date of the notice. I am submitting it through my.cigna.com (or by calling 1-800-244-6224 / the number on my card), using the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

---

## What the plan's own guideline says, and what my records show

The Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 guideline opens the total hip replacement section this way:

> "Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Total Hip Replacement Indications CMM.JT.IN.313 v1.0.2026 Total hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

and, in the same guideline:

> "hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met:"

**A note about what I am quoting.** The only guideline text I quote in this letter is text I have in front of me, word for word. The portions of CMM-313 I have been able to quote are the general introductory language above and the functional and conservative-care criteria set out below. I have **not** been given, and therefore do not quote, the guideline's specific indication language for degenerative joint disease of the hip. Where I discuss how my imaging fits that indication, I am describing my records in my own words, not the plan's. My imaging shows degenerative change — it does not show a fracture or avascular necrosis — and I am not claiming otherwise.

### 1. Function-limiting pain at short distances, for at least three months

The guideline states:

> "◦ function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration ▪ Criteria exception:"

**My records establish this.** The clinical summary in the prior authorization packet documents **24 months** of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest. It documents that I ambulate **with a cane and am limited to one block** — less than the two-city-block example the guideline itself gives. Twenty-four months is well beyond the three-month duration the criterion requires.

### 2. Loss of hip function affecting daily activities, and failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three months

The guideline states:

> "◦ loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration ◦ Criteria exception:"

**My records establish both halves of this.**

*Loss of function affecting activities of daily living:* the packet documents that I **cannot put on my shoes unassisted** and that I walk with a cane, limited to one block. Examination documents **positive provocative testing on the affected side** and **range of motion limited by pain**.

*Failure of provider-directed, non-surgical management for at least three months:* the packet documents, with dates and a discharge note —

| What the guideline asks for | What my records contain |
|---|---|
| Provider-directed non-surgical management | **Supervised physical therapy**, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait: **16 weeks, 2026-03-03 to 2026-06-23, 20 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note |
| Lasting at least three months | 16 weeks — longer than three months |
| Failure of that management | **NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief**; **corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-15 giving only 3 weeks of partial relief**; pain remains progressive and unrelieved by rest |

Because I completed more than three months of supervised, provider-directed non-surgical care and it failed, the guideline's exception provisions — which read "Three (3) months of function-limiting pain is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate," "Three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical management is not required when the medical record clearly documents why provider-directed non-surgical management is inappropriate," "Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate," and "The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate" — are not something I need to rely on. I met the three-month requirement directly.

### 3. Objective imaging and the absence of contraindications

My imaging of **2026-06-02**, a weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph, shows **joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes**. The packet also documents **no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker status**.

---

## On the stated reason for the denial

The notice does not identify a particular clinical criterion that my records fail to meet. It states only that the documentation was incomplete. The material summarized above — dated imaging, a dated and quantified course of physical therapy with a discharge note, dated medication and injection trials with the response to each, specific functional limits, and examination findings — was part of the prior authorization packet submitted by my surgeon's office.

If any specific document is missing from Cigna's file, I am asking that the reviewer identify it in writing so my surgeon's office can send it directly. I would also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with expertise in orthopedic surgery.

---

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask that Cigna overturn the denial dated 2026-08-09 and authorize the total hip replacement (CPT 27130) requested by Lindqvist, MD. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the specific criterion of the Cigna CMM-313 Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 guideline that my records are found not to meet, along with information about my further appeal rights, including any right to an external review.

I have enclosed the records referenced above and authorize my surgeon's office to release any additional documentation Cigna requests.

Thank you for taking the time to look at this again.

Sincerely,

**Emerson Alvarez**
Member ID: W977514824
Reference number: POC-4E415360FE-32022
[Signature]
